crazygames.name: CrazyGames
crazygames.audience: Large browser-game audience, strong on desktop; says it strongly supports online multiplayer (2x long-term retention).
crazygames.revenue: Ad revenue share via its SDK; in-game purchases invite-only (Xsolla). No general split published; its 2026 jam terms gave 60% ads / 70% purchases (jam-specific).
crazygames.exclusivity: Not required for a normal launch.
crazygames.requirements: CrazyGames SDK (ads only through it); Basic Launch then Full Launch after QA and benchmarks; multiplayer: show usernames, instant-multiplayer flag, lobby sizes; any chat needs a profanity filter.
crazygames.process: Self-serve: developer dashboard, upload the build, metadata and assets, review.
crazygames.fitNotes: Best match: 1v1 online plus a bot, desktop-first, strategy. Bottle messages are free text: add a profanity filter. Show both captains' names (already shown).
crazygames.nextAction: Read the requirements and plan the SDK integration

poki.name: Poki
poki.audience: One of the largest web-game portals; strong on mobile and young players.
poki.revenue: Players Poki brings: 50/50; players you bring: 100% yours. One-time licence fee as a non-exclusive alternative.
poki.exclusivity: Deals ask for web exclusivity, 5 years by default (Steam and app stores stay open).
poki.requirements: Poki SDK; their requirements page (check initial download size: an unverified guide says under 8 MB); curated: starts with a 'web fit test'.
poki.process: Apply through the developer portal (web fit test), then curation.
poki.fitNotes: Strong reach, but web exclusivity would close the other portals, and Poki leans to mobile, which the game does not support. Decide after CrazyGames.
poki.nextAction: Take the web fit test; weigh exclusivity

discord.name: Discord Activities
discord.audience: Friends playing together inside Discord voice and text channels, on desktop, web and mobile.
discord.revenue: In-app purchases through Discord; no ad network.
discord.requirements: Embedded App SDK: the web game runs in an iframe inside Discord; Discord sign-in; requests go through Discord's URL mapping.
discord.process: Self-serve: create an app in the Developer Portal, build the Activity, then apply for discovery.
discord.fitNotes: 1v1 between friends in a channel is exactly the social case. Needs work: Discord identity instead of room codes, and the iframe proxy for Firebase.
discord.nextAction: Prototype an Activity with a room per channel

armorgames.name: Armor Games
armorgames.audience: Long-standing core audience for strategy and quality browser games.
armorgames.revenue: Deals such as branding for a fee, or timed site exclusivity ('one of the highest paying options').
armorgames.requirements: HTML5 only; multiplayer games may be hosted in an iframe.
armorgames.process: Through the developer site; no public form found. Its publishing studio laid off staff in 2024.
armorgames.fitNotes: Audience that likes strategy and polish. A good place for a sponsorship pitch by e-mail.
armorgames.nextAction: Find the current developer contact and send the pitch

gamedistribution.name: GameDistribution (Azerion)
gamedistribution.audience: Puts the game on thousands of partner sites at once.
gamedistribution.revenue: 33% of net revenue to the developer (its developer agreement).
gamedistribution.fitNotes: Wide but thin reach; partner sites embed the game, so online play must work inside any iframe.
gamedistribution.nextAction: After CrazyGames: add its SDK as a build variant

playgama.name: Playgama
playgama.audience: Network of portals reached through one 'Bridge' SDK.
playgama.revenue: Advertises about 80% to the developer; $100 payout threshold (its own claims, to verify).
playgama.process: Self-serve; says it tests and replies within 24 hours.
playgama.fitNotes: One SDK for several portals; check the numbers in their terms before relying on them.

gamepix.name: GamePix
gamepix.audience: Own portal plus a distribution network.
gamepix.fitNotes: Secondary channel once one SDK integration exists.

y8.name: Y8
y8.revenue: About 50% ad share (portal comparisons); a 'studio' is needed only to earn.
y8.requirements: Y8 developer account and App ID; HTML5/WebGL.

yandex.name: Yandex Games
yandex.audience: Very large in Russian-speaking countries and Türkiye.
yandex.revenue: Licence plus ad revenue under its publishing agreement (split not found).
yandex.requirements: Yandex Games SDK for ads and payments; playable without signing in elsewhere; moderation 3 to 5 working days.
yandex.fitNotes: Big audience, but it would want Russian (and Turkish) text and its own SDK; sign-in to Firebase accounts must stay optional (it already is).

itch.name: itch.io
itch.audience: Indie players and developers; good for feedback, devlogs and jams.
itch.revenue: Free or pay-what-you-want; you choose itch.io's share.
itch.requirements: Upload the build (or link the site); a page with screenshots.
itch.fitNotes: Quick first presence and a home for devlogs; low revenue, high feedback.
itch.nextAction: Make the page with screenshots and the trailer

newgrounds.name: Newgrounds
newgrounds.audience: Long-running creative community that votes on games.
newgrounds.revenue: Little: no published HTML5 ad share (Newgrounds.io API for medals and scores).
newgrounds.requirements: Zip with index.html at the root.

famobi.name: Famobi
famobi.audience: Licenses games to publishers and brands.
famobi.requirements: Famobi SDK; mostly casual and mobile titles.
famobi.fitNotes: Leans to casual mobile games; a long shot.

coolmath.name: Coolmath Games
coolmath.requirements: Every game reviewed by staff; no shooter or violent games; no mature content.
coolmath.process: Developer portal form; licensing talks reported at games@coolmath.com (unofficial).
coolmath.fitNotes: Strategy fits, but naval cannon fire and ships sinking may count as violent; chat-like bottle notes are a risk for children.

kongregate.name: Kongregate
kongregate.process: Reported to no longer accept game submissions.
kongregate.fitNotes: Closed to new games: kept here only so it is not researched again.

approach.name: First approach
approach.subject: The Sunken Covenant — a 1v1 naval strategy game for {{portal}}
approach.body:
Hi {{contact}},

I'm Daniel Moya, the developer of The Sunken Covenant, a turn-based 1v1 naval strategy game for the browser, and I think it could be a good fit for {{portal}}.

Two captains hide their fleets on 16×16 charts and fight it out with action points, a hand of order cards and the weather: wind that helps or stops square-rigged ships, storms, a closing maelstrom, and a Kraken summoned with covenant seals. Five commanders change how each battle plays. Everything is rendered in 3D with an engraved, hand-inked look.

- Play now: https://the-sunken-covenant.web.app
- Online 1v1 with a room code, or against the computer
- Guided first battle; English and Spanish
- Desktop browsers; plain three.js and TypeScript, no plugins
- Fairness built in: every online battle is verified from both captains' logs at the end

I'd love to know whether it fits {{portal}}, and what you would need from me: SDK integration, build size, exclusivity terms or anything else. I'm happy to adapt the build.

Thank you for your time,

Daniel Moya Teruel
soymachine@gmail.com
https://the-sunken-covenant.web.app
